article.title: NFL EDGE Tuesday Evening Brief
article.dek: Lamar Jackson is likely out Sunday night, the market flipped six points on Ravens–Falcons, and the evening refresh swapped two of the three headline cards.

items.headline: Lamar Jackson is likely out Sunday night — and the market already flipped
paragraphs: The day's biggest news: Lamar Jackson has only an 'outside chance' to play Sunday night in Atlanta, per Ian Rapoport on Tuesday morning. The ankle sprain that knocked him out of the second half against Tennessee on Sunday could cost him multiple games. Tyler Huntley would start for the Ravens.
The market didn't wait. This morning the board had Baltimore -2.5. Tonight it's Atlanta -3.5 on DraftKings and -3.0 on FanDuel — about a six-point swing on one quarterback's ankle.

One catch: the app still lists Lamar Jackson as Baltimore's expected starter. The feed hasn't caught up to the Rapoport report. Don't bet a Ravens number the model priced with Lamar in it — run your book's price through Check first.
items.takeaway: The news beat the feed on the day's biggest move. Use Check until the app knows who's starting.

items.headline: Washington: the plan is Jayden Daniels on Sunday — the app doesn't know yet
paragraphs: Jayden Daniels is on track to start against the Giants on Sunday. Dan Quinn said Monday the goal is a full week of practice and a start, after Daniels sat out since dislocating his elbow in Week 2.
The rest of the room: Marcus Mariota sprained his MCL again in London and is expected to miss time. If Daniels can't go, it's rookie Athan Kaliakmanis — 186 yards and a pick in relief on Sunday.

The line has come back to Washington -3.5 at both books, in line with the market expecting Daniels. But the app still shows Kaliakmanis as the expected starter. Same rule as Baltimore: the news beat the feed, so run your price through Check.
items.takeaway: Washington's quarterback picture is clearing up — the app just hasn't heard yet.

items.headline: Giants: Dart is done for the season — it's Winston's team now
paragraphs: Jaxson Dart is out for the season with a knee injury. Jameis Winston starts for the 3-1 Giants in Washington on Sunday.
No mystery left here: the app has Winston locked in, and the -3.5 line already assumes Daniels on the other side.
items.takeaway: Winston vs. (probably) Daniels on Sunday afternoon.

items.headline: No weather to handicap
paragraphs: Thursday night's game is at AT&T Stadium in Arlington — a dome, so the weather does nothing. Sunday kickoff-window weather gets a proper look in the morning brief.
items.takeaway: Weather is a non-factor for Thursday; Sunday's outdoor games get checked in the morning.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The Hit Rate card is Denver now — likeliest winner, not best price
paragraphs: The evening refresh swapped the Hit Rate card: Jacksonville is out, Denver moneyline at -185 on DraftKings is in. The model gives the Broncos a 62.4% chance at the Chargers, 0.5 units, medium reliability.

Remember what this card is: the pick the app thinks is most likely to win — the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. The expected value here is slightly negative. That's by design, not a flaw.
items.takeaway: Play the Hit Rate card for what it is: the likeliest winner on the board, not the best price.

items.headline: The Balanced card is Minnesota — strong pick, reasonable price
paragraphs: Also new tonight: Minnesota moneyline at -130 on DraftKings replaces Buffalo +2.5. The model has the Vikings at 69.4% against the Saints, 0.75 units, low reliability.
Balanced is the middle lane: a strong pick without paying too much. If you're new, this is the sensible starting point — good win probability, sane price.
items.takeaway: Balanced means what it says: strong pick, fair price. Minnesota -130.

items.headline: The Value card still found the Raiders — and still refuses to bet them
paragraphs: The model's only +EV play is unchanged: Raiders moneyline at +176 on FanDuel. Model 46.5%, market 36.7%, expected value +1.7%, low reliability. It's still a watch, not a bet — the card only fires at +184 or better.
That's the Value lane doing its job: it's the always-+EV play, and right now +176 isn't the number. If the price drifts to +184, it becomes a bet. Until then, it waits.
items.takeaway: The only +EV play on the board is the Raiders — at +184, not +176.

items.headline: Baltimore–Atlanta flipped six points on the Lamar news
paragraphs: Morning: Ravens -2.5 on DraftKings. Tonight: Falcons -3.5 on DraftKings, -3.0 on FanDuel. That's the market pricing in Tyler Huntley instead of Lamar Jackson.

The model's own number has Atlanta by about 2.9 — a touch below the -3.5 market price. But the model was built on its quarterback feed, which still says Lamar Jackson. When the news beats the feed, the model number is stale too. Tap Check, type in your book's line, and get a verdict on your actual price.
items.takeaway: The biggest move of the day is fully explained by one ankle. Check is how you bet it cleanly.

items.headline: Washington back to -3.5 as the Daniels plan firms up
paragraphs: The Commanders drifted to -3.0 this morning on quarterback uncertainty. Tonight they're back at -3.5 at both books — the market believes Daniels starts.
Direction of the next move depends on the practice reports. If Daniels is full-go all week, this number holds. Any setback and it slides back.
items.takeaway: The market has priced in the Daniels return. Practice reports move this next.

items.headline: Dallas–Tampa moved toward the Bucs ahead of Thursday night
paragraphs: Cowboys -9.5 this morning, -8.5 tonight at both books, total steady at 47.5. A full point toward Tampa Bay with the undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels starting for the Bucs.

Kickoff is Thursday at 8:15 p.m. ET in Arlington. If your book isn't showing -8.5, run your number through Check — it re-runs the model and the evaluator on your price and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict.
items.takeaway: A point of movement toward Tampa Bay before Thursday night.

items.headline: Jacksonville -6.5 to -7 against the Eagles
paragraphs: A quiet half-point toward the Jaguars in the London game. Small move, no news attached — the kind of drift that usually just means money, not information.
items.takeaway: Half a point to Jacksonville, nothing more to read into.

items.headline: Two card swaps on the evening refresh
paragraphs: The 6:00 p.m. refresh replaced two of the three headline cards: Hit Rate went from Jacksonville moneyline to Denver moneyline (-185), and Balanced went from Buffalo +2.5 to Minnesota moneyline (-130). The Value card is unchanged — still the Raiders at +176, still waiting on +184.
These aren't market moves; they're the board updating its own recommendations on fresh prices. Tonight's cards are tonight's numbers, not this morning's.
items.takeaway: The board refreshes every morning and evening — tonight's picks replaced this morning's.

items.headline: Practical tip: Thursday game? Thursday check.
paragraphs: Buccaneers at Cowboys kicks off Thursday at 8:15 p.m. ET. Before you bet it, open the app, tap Check, and type in your book's line and price. The app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and hands you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price — a full re-evaluation, not a guess.
Read the odds as price mechanics: -110 means every $1.10 you risk wins $1. Your actual stake lives in the app, sized from your bankroll and your staking setting.
items.takeaway: Thursday game? Thursday check. Bet your book's number, not the board's.

items.headline: Jargon: reverse line movement (and why there's no Fade tonight)
paragraphs: Reverse line movement is when the line moves toward one team while most of the bets pile onto the other side — the classic shape a Fade watches for. A real Fade needs that split verified: tickets on one side, money on the other, plus a line move to back it up.
Tonight the free VSiN tier only showed college football splits — no NFL row to read. No verified split, no Fade. That's the rule working as designed.
items.takeaway: A Fade needs tickets and money pointing opposite ways, verified — not vibes. Tonight: no split, no Fade.

evidence.fact: Lamar Jackson (ankle sprain, sat out the 2nd half of Baltimore's Week 4 win over Tennessee) has only an 'outside chance' to play Sunday night at Atlanta, per Ian Rapoport (NFL Network, reported Tuesday morning Oct 6). Rapoport adds Jackson could miss multiple games depending on rehab; the injury is not considered long-term or surgical. Tyler Huntley would start for the Ravens if Jackson sits. Ravens coach Jesse Minter would not estimate Jackson's chances Monday.

Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Monday (Oct 5) the goal is for Jayden Daniels (dislocated left elbow, out since Week 2) to practice all week and start Sunday vs the Giants. Marcus Mariota sprained his MCL (the same knee injured in the preseason opener) in the first quarter of the Week 4 London loss to the Colts and is expected to miss time; rookie Athan Kaliakmanis (7th round, Rutgers) is the fallback — 15-of-33, 186 yds, 1 TD, 1 INT in relief Sunday. Gary Myers reports Daniels is expected to start vs the Giants.
Jaxson Dart (NYG) is out for the season with a knee injury; veteran Jameis Winston starts for the 3-1 Giants.
